Container.Name: BuilderBot
Container.Overview:
Claude Code workstation + self-hosted GitHub Actions runner + Playwright + Android SDK/emulator in one container.
Use it from a terminal: docker exec -it BuilderBot claude Helper CLI inside: docker exec -it BuilderBot bb status
NOTES - The image is a private GHCR package: run `docker login ghcr.io` on the Unraid host once (and persist it via the go file) or the pull will fail. See docs/unraid.md in the repo. - Extra Params ship as --hostname=builderbot --device=/dev/kvm --runtime=nvidia because that is the host this template was written for. BOTH OF THOSE FAIL THE CONTAINER OUTRIGHT ON HARDWARE THAT LACKS THEM - docker refuses to start with "unknown or invalid runtime name: nvidia", or "no such file or directory" for /dev/kvm. If your server has no NVIDIA GPU, or virtualization is off, delete the matching flag from Extra Params before hitting Apply. - --runtime=nvidia also needs the Nvidia-Driver plugin from Apps (Unraid 6.9+). Leave NVIDIA_DRIVER_CAPABILITIES at "all": the runtime default gives you CUDA but no GL/EGL/Vulkan, which fails in a way that still looks healthy in nvidia-smi. Confirm with: docker exec -it BuilderBot bb doctor - The Android emulator is ON by default and needs the /dev/kvm device above. Set ENABLE_ANDROID_EMULATOR to false for a pure workstation; nothing starts automatically either way (use: bb emu start). - The Docker socket mapping is OFF by default: mounting it gives the container root-equivalent control of the Unraid host. Fill in the socket path only if you accept that and want docker build/compose available inside.

Config.Name: Projects folder
Config.Description: The folder your projects live in. Every subfolder becomes a project at /workspace/<name> - add one by creating a folder here, no container edit needed. Anything wrong with a folder (no git repository, no CLAUDE.md, wrong ownership) is reported on the dashboard rather than hidden. The runner's _work directory sits inside this share and is skipped in every project list.

Config.Name: Home (Claude login, shell config)
Config.Description: Persists Claude Code credentials, npm globals, AVDs and shell history across image updates

Config.Name: Config (custom startup hooks)
Config.Description: Drop your own *.sh files into startup.d/ here to run them at container start

Config.Name: Runner work directory
Config.Description: Everything the GitHub Actions runner owns: job checkouts, the toolchains setup-node/python/java download, and its diagnostics. Kept apart from the SDK share so a workflow cannot bump a version out from under your sessions. Safe to empty when no job is running; the runner rebuilds it.

Config.Name: Logs directory (optional override)
Config.Description: Leave empty to keep logs under the Config path in logs/. Set a host path (e.g. an array share like /mnt/user/logs/builderbot) to send the persistent log there instead - the container auto-detects this mount.

Config.Name: Secrets directory (shielded tokens)
Config.Description: RECOMMENDED: a root-owned host folder (chmod 700) containing builderbot.env with GITHUB_PAT=... lines, plus an ssh/ subfolder of git private keys. Secrets provided this way are never readable by Claude sessions - the runner gets tokens via a root-only helper and ssh keys are served by a root-owned ssh-agent (usable for git push, not extractable). See docs/unraid.md.

Config.Name: SDK share (large toolchains)
Config.Description: RECOMMENDED: where the big downloadable toolchains live - Android platforms, build-tools, the emulator and its system images, the Playwright browsers, plus Flutter, .NET and Swift if you install them. Keeping them here means an image update never re-downloads them. Manage with: bb sdk. Leave empty and they fall back to the home volume, which persists too but mixes gigabytes in with your shell history.

Config.Name: Scanner reports (read-only)
Config.Description: Optional: the output directory of a static analyzer running on the host, e.g. /mnt/user/appdata/scanners/reports. Mounted READ-ONLY and deliberately without the scanner itself, so nothing in this container can run or reconfigure it. Read the reports with: bb findings

Config.Name: Unraid icon cache
Config.Description: Optional, cosmetic: Unraid's own icon cache. Mounted here, the container writes its icon in on every start, so the Docker page shows one without downloading anything - which is what fails while this repo is private. Set UNRAID_ICON_NAME if you renamed the container. Leave empty for Unraid's placeholder.

Config.Name: Docker socket (OFF by default - root-equivalent!)
Config.Description: LEAVE EMPTY unless you accept the risk: mounting the host Docker socket lets anything in this container run arbitrary code on the Unraid host as root. Set to /var/run/docker.sock only if you want Claude/CI jobs building images against the host daemon. PREFER the Docker proxy address variable below, which reaches the daemon through a filtering proxy instead.

Config.Name: Docker daemon (dev instances)
Config.Description: Which daemon the dashboard's dev-instance controls drive. Two arrangements: a sandbox VM's own daemon over ssh (ssh://user@vm), which is the safer one because that machine holds nothing - see docs/sandbox-vm.md - or a socket proxy on this box. 'auto' finds a running docker-socket-proxy on this container's network and re-finds it when its address moves; an explicit tcp://172.17.0.1:2375 is used verbatim; empty turns the feature off. docs/unraid.md has the proxy's allowlist.

Config.Name: Dev container name prefix
Config.Description: The namespace every dev-instance compose project is named in, so a container the dashboard made is called bbdev-myapp rather than myapp. It is not decoration: the dashboard refuses any compose call outside this prefix, and when the daemon is this box's - a socket proxy, or the mounted socket - that refusal is the only thing stopping it acting on one of your real containers, because a proxy's flags are per endpoint and cannot tell one container from another. Set it to the word none (or leave it empty) to drop the prefix and have containers named exactly what you typed - the word is the reliable spelling, because a blanked template field can come back holding this Default again. That is honoured only when the Docker daemon above is a sandbox VM (ssh://), where the machine holds nothing worth protecting; anywhere else an empty value falls back to bbdev.

Config.Name: Host path mapping (dev instances)
Config.Description: What this container's paths are called on whichever machine runs the daemon, as /here:/there pairs. Bind-mount sources are resolved over there, and docker answers a missing one by creating an empty directory instead of failing. Shipped as the sandbox-VM value /workspace:/workspace, where both sides use the same path. For a daemon on THIS box, name the host's path instead: /workspace:/mnt/user/development/projects. Pairs are checked against this container's mounts and a wrong one is flagged on the project's row.

Config.Name: Dev instance data (its own share)
Config.Description: Where a dev instance's volumes live. A project's compose opts in with ${BB_DEV_DATA}/... and the dashboard points that at a per-instance folder under this path. Give it a SHARE of its own rather than a folder inside appdata: Unraid exports and backs up shares, not folders, so data under appdata cannot be handed to the sandbox VM or backed up without dragging every other container's configuration with it - and the sandbox mounts this one over NFS. Speed is that share's own cache setting, not something to pin into this path. Needed for a daemon on THIS box - a socket proxy or the mounted socket - because BuilderBot has to make that folder itself and can only do it through a mount. With a sandbox VM, leave this EMPTY: that machine mounts the share and makes the folder, and a mount here is not merely spare - it makes BuilderBot use its own copy of the path instead, which then needs a /devdata pair in the host path mapping as well or the variable is left unset and the compose refuses to start.

Config.Name: TZ
Config.Description: Container timezone

Config.Name: PUID
Config.Description: File-owner uid (99 = Unraid's nobody)

Config.Name: PGID
Config.Description: File-owner gid (100 = Unraid's users)

Config.Name: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
Config.Description: Optional: API-key billing. Leave empty to log in with a Claude subscription instead (docker exec -it BuilderBot bb login, one time).

Config.Name: AUTO_UPDATE_CLAUDE
Config.Description: Update Claude Code on every container start

Config.Name: GITHUB_URL
Config.Description: Org URL (https://github.com/ORG) serves every repo in the org and needs the PAT permission Organization - Self-hosted runners: R/W. A repo URL (https://github.com/OWNER/REPO) serves one repo and needs Repository - Administration: R/W instead.

Config.Name: GITHUB_PAT
Config.Description: Fine-grained PAT with Administration read+write on the target repo. NOTE: any variable set here is visible to processes inside the container (including Claude sessions) - prefer the Secrets directory mount for shielding. Values are always redacted from logs either way.

Config.Name: ENABLE_RUNNER
Config.Description: Set false to run as a pure Claude workstation

Config.Name: GIT_PAT (for git/gh inside)
Config.Description: Token for git clone/push and the gh CLI inside the container. Unlike GITHUB_PAT it is readable by sessions - anything git can use, a session can read - so scope it to repository Contents (read/write) only, never Administration. A shielded ssh key in /secrets/ssh is the alternative.

Config.Name: RUNNER_NAME
Config.Description: Runner name shown in GitHub

Config.Name: RUNNER_LABELS
Config.Description: Labels workflows target with runs-on

Config.Name: RUNNER_EPHEMERAL
Config.Description: Fresh registration per job (recommended)

Config.Name: RUNNER_GROUP
Config.Description: Runner group (org-level runners only)

Config.Name: CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION
Config.Description: Pin a Claude Code version for the startup auto-update

Config.Name: GIT_USER_NAME
Config.Description: git commit author name

Config.Name: GIT_USER_EMAIL
Config.Description: git commit author email. The GitHub noreply address attributes commits to your profile without publishing a real address, and survives the "block pushes that expose my email" setting.

Config.Name: ENABLE_ANDROID_EMULATOR
Config.Description: Create an AVD per API level in ANDROID_SYSTEM_IMAGES at startup. Needs --device=/dev/kvm in Extra Params (pre-set). Start one with: bb emu start

Config.Name: ANDROID_SYSTEM_IMAGES
Config.Description: Comma-separated API levels to keep an emulator image and AVD for, e.g. 34,35,36,37 for Android 14 through 17. Budget ~2GB each on the appdata share - downloaded once, kept across image updates. AVDs are named builderbot-<api>; boot one with: bb emu start 37

Config.Name: ENABLE_GPU_DISPLAY
Config.Description: Start a headless X server at boot for a passed-through NVIDIA GPU, so the Android emulator can render on it. Does nothing without a GPU. NVIDIA_DRIVER_CAPABILITIES must include display (all does).

Config.Name: ANDROID_EMULATOR_GPU
Config.Description: Emulator renderer. Leave empty to auto-detect: the container starts an X server for a passed-through NVIDIA GPU and uses it if EGL agrees, falling back to software otherwise. Set swiftshader_indirect or swangle_indirect to force software, or host to insist on the GPU.

Config.Name: NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES
Config.Description: Nvidia GPU UUID. Requires the Nvidia-Driver plugin and --runtime=nvidia in Extra Params. all is fine for a single card; with several, paste the UUID from Settings - Nvidia-Driver (e.g. GPU-7f326d12-d4c8-4011-9db1-36c47710daf6).

Config.Name: NVIDIA_DRIVER_CAPABILITIES
Config.Description: Only applies with --runtime=nvidia in Extra Params. Leave at all: the runtime default (compute,utility) injects CUDA but no GL/EGL/Vulkan, so hardware rendering fails while nvidia-smi still looks healthy.

Config.Name: ENABLE_DASHBOARD
Config.Description: Web dashboard: container and runner status, bb macro buttons, and a browser terminal with a persistent tmux session per project. Needs DASHBOARD_AUTH set or it will not start.

Config.Name: DASHBOARD_AUTH
Config.Description: REQUIRED when the dashboard is enabled, as user:password. The dashboard serves a writable shell inside this container, which holds your loaded ssh-agent and read-write mounts of every project - so treat this credential as equivalent to those. With it empty the dashboard refuses to start and says so in the log.

Config.Name: Dashboard port
Config.Description: Web UI for the dashboard page.

Config.Name: DASHBOARD_MAX_TABS
Config.Description: How many dashboard tabs may be open at once. Each terminal tab is an iframe running a full terminal emulator over its own websocket, so this is a ceiling on browser memory rather than a tidiness rule - a phone hits it well before a desktop does. The tab strip is stored on the container and shared by every browser that opens the dashboard.

Config.Name: DASHBOARD_DOCTOR_INTERVAL
Config.Description: How often the dashboard re-runs bb doctor in the background, in seconds (minimum 300). The Doctor card's refresh re-runs it on demand regardless.

Config.Name: DASHBOARD_PORT
Config.Description: Must match the Dashboard port mapping above.

Config.Name: DASHBOARD_TTYD_PORT
Config.Description: The LOOPBACK port ttyd binds to inside the container. The browser never talks to it - terminals are proxied through the dashboard port under /term, behind the same single sign-in - so it needs no port mapping. Leave at 7681.

Config.Name: SDK_ROOT
Config.Description: Where downloadable SDKs are kept inside the container. Leave at /sdk; it pairs with the SDK share mapping above. With no share mapped the SDKs fall back to the home volume, which persists too but mixes them in with everything else.

Config.Name: NPM_TOKEN
Config.Description: Optional: auth token for npm publish to registry.npmjs.org

Config.Name: SHIELD_SECRETS
Config.Description: Scrub GITHUB_PAT/RUNNER_TOKEN from session environments; the runner mints tokens via a root-only helper instead. Set false only for legacy behavior (PAT visible inside, gh auto-authenticated).

Config.Name: EXTRA_APT_PACKAGES
Config.Description: Space-separated apt packages installed at every start

Config.Name: EXTRA_NPM_PACKAGES
Config.Description: Space-separated global npm packages installed at every start

Config.Name: EXTRA_PIPX_PACKAGES
Config.Description: Space-separated pipx tools installed at every start

Config.Name: PROJECT_BOOTSTRAP
Config.Description: Run each project's .builderbot/setup.sh at start

Config.Name: CHOWN_PROJECTS
Config.Description: Recursively chown project mounts to PUID:PGID at start

Config.Name: BB_SESSION_HISTORY
Config.Description: How many lines of each terminal's scrollback are saved at shutdown and printed back on restore. Bigger means larger files under the Config path in sessions/. What was RUNNING in a terminal is not restored - that went down with the container.

Config.Name: BB_LOG_KEEP
Config.Description: A ceiling on how many boots of logs are kept, not the retention policy. How long logs are kept is a number of DAYS, set in the dashboard's settings menu (the gear) and 30 by default. This exists only so a container in a crash loop cannot fill the log directory before that policy gets a chance to apply.

Config.Name: SHUTDOWN_GRACE
Config.Description: Seconds a stop may spend shutting down cleanly - deregistering the runner, powering the emulator off, ending Claude sessions. IMPORTANT: Unraid kills the container after its own Docker Stop Timeout (Settings -> Docker, 10s by default) regardless, so raise that or this has no room to run.

Config.Name: UNRAID_ICON_NAME
Config.Description: Only matters with the Unraid icon cache mapping. Unraid names the cached icon after the CONTAINER, and nothing inside a container can see its own container name - so if you renamed this container from BuilderBot, put the new name here or the icon lands under the wrong filename and is ignored.
